name: Instagram Face

image.caption: I was using Instagram’s face filters on things in the house and I’m so pleased with this addition to my Vallejo print.

lead: Instagram face is a name for a recurring look seen among social-media beauty figures: catlike eyes, a small nose, high cheekbones, full lips and smooth, even skin. People who want the look use makeup, filters and cosmetic procedures such as fillers or neurotoxin.

The term was used by Jia Tolentino in The New Yorker in 2019. A 2024 study measured facial proportions of 100 top beauty influencers to see whether an ideal Instagram face could be described numerically.

paras: Practitioners describe reaching the look through contouring and lash makeup, filters, and in-person treatments such as lip filler and neurotoxin injections, with surgeons reporting patients bringing filtered selfies as references.

Critics describe homogenised beauty standards, and procedures carry their own risks such as swelling, bruising and dissatisfaction. Meta agreed to restrict extreme makeup filters for minors in 2026 according to Wikipedia.

angle.text: People use the description as a styling and treatment target, from contouring to fillers; it is also a template debated as a homogenised ideal.

lead: Instagram face is a term for a standardised facial aesthetic associated with social-media beauty influencers: high cheekbones, full lips, a small nose, large cat-like eyes and smooth skin. Wikipedia says Jia Tolentino used the phrase in The New Yorker in 2019 and named Kim Kardashian its patient zero.[1]

The look begins with digital filters but is pursued in person through heavy makeup or cosmetic treatments such as Botox and fillers. Wikipedia notes Kylie Jenner's 2015 lip-filler confession as a moment that introduced Juvederm to a new generation.[1]

A 2024 cross-sectional study in Aesthetic Surgery Journal Open Forum analysed facial proportions of 100 top female beauty influencers, assessing lip ratio, Ricketts' line and nasal dimensions against golden-ratio standards.[2]
infobox: High cheekbones, full lips, small nose, cat eyes

paras: Described traits include catlike eyes, long lashes, a small nose, high cheekbones, full lips and a blank expression, and Tolentino described the face as distinctly white but ambiguously ethnic.[1]

Wikipedia reports Americans had 7 million neurotoxin and 2.5 million filler injections in 2018. Critics say filters produce a homogeneous standard; Claire Raymond argues in a 2021 book that it erases heritable quirks and lived history. Surgeon Paul Banwell noted in 2024 that patients increasingly want to look like their filtered selves.[1]

A 2024 cross-sectional observational study measured facial proportions in the 100 top female beauty influencers (mean age 31.3) to identify an ideal Instagram face and compare with the golden ratio.[2] No treatment trials of the look as such were found.
